tasks.short: Assign public relations work, review its quality and coach the team.

steps.what: Collect deadlines, work status and team availability.
Choose owners, priorities and deadlines for incoming work.
Brief staff, clarify expectations and remove delivery obstacles.
Review submitted work and decide what needs revision.
Discuss performance, provide coaching and agree development actions.
Update task records and send deadline reminders.

tasks.design: Configure a shared queue, workload view and decision-triggered reminders in the {PROJECT}, using availability from the {CALENDAR}. Link work to its brief and review decision in the {DOCS}; keep confidential development records separate in the {TALENT}. The manager assigns work, judges quality and coaches staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefs, review comments and deadlines are disconnected. Existing features often remain unused because team practices and record ownership are inconsistent.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured views and status-triggered workflows cover most coordination. Small integrations are easier to build and maintain with AI-assisted coding; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Capacity depends on experience, hidden work and wellbeing. GDPR and national rules affect employee records and consultation; adding employee evaluation AI would require a separate EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Judge fairness, give difficult feedback and develop people without reducing performance to activity counts.

ambition.what: Make a weekly capacity and development trade-off before accepting new work.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing status and more time reviewing work and coaching. They can rebalance assignments within existing authority; employment decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Create a shared editorial review rubric for public relations content.
reach.learn: Learn how to distinguish factual accuracy, audience fit and editorial preference in feedback.

evidence.claim: Configured work queues, review states and reminders can reduce manual coordination without employee scoring.
The supplied digest contains no documented case proving automated public relations staff supervision.

assumptions: Staff maintain task status as part of delivery rather than receiving separate status requests.
Existing availability records are sufficient; the design adds no behavioural monitoring.
Time shares and remaining time are estimates; the modest gain reflects the human-heavy task.
Access estimates include employee consultation under applicable national rules; formal processes may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether a shared work queue already exists and is consistently used.
Which workload and development records the manager may see.
Whether employee representatives must be consulted about the proposed views.
Who may approve reassignment, overtime and external resources.
research_questions: Which status requests can disappear once the shared queue is reliable?
Do reminders help delivery or create avoidable notification load?
Does the workload view expose hidden work without encouraging activity-based evaluation?
new_work: Maintain task states, ownership and reminder rules.
Resolve missing or misleading status data.
Review workload views with staff for fairness and usefulness.
Maintain separation between delivery records and confidential coaching records.
tasks.statement: Assign, supervise, and review the activities of public relations staff.

tasks.short: Agree employee communications with labor relations managers, then prepare, approve and distribute updates.

steps.what: Collect approved activity updates, workforce questions and communication constraints.
Agree messages, timing and employee concerns with the labor relations manager.
Write the employee update and supporting supervisor notes.

loop.input: Agreed communication brief, approved updates and employee communication templates.
loop.output: Employee update draft and supervisor notes with source references.
loop.check: Check dates, promises, audience, confidentiality and consistency with the agreed brief.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved employment implications return to the labor relations manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sensitive updates need clear wording adapted to employee concerns.

steps.what: Approve employment wording, release timing and audience.
Publish the approved update and distribute supervisor notes.
Collate employee questions from the shared mailbox.

loop.input: Employee questions with unnecessary identifiers removed.
loop.output: Question log grouped by topic, with restricted links to originals.
loop.check: Check topic coverage; separate personal cases; prohibit employee sentiment or performance scores.
loop.stop: One grouping pass per batch; ambiguous and personal cases go to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Employees express the same concern in different free-text forms.

steps.what: Discuss unresolved concerns and agree follow-up answers with the labor relations manager.

tasks.design: A briefing generator on {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles approved updates from {DOCS} and {PROJECT}, while a bounded drafting loop prepares employee updates and supervisor notes. People agree the message and employment implications; {WORKFLOW} publishes through {DOCS} and {EMAIL} only after approval and groups incoming questions for human follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts, wording decisions and approval threads were separated. Employee communications also depend on trust and employment context that templates cannot settle.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates, access-controlled retrieval and approval flows are established techniques. AI-assisted coding makes their assembly cheaper, while bounded drafting reduces first-draft effort.
tasks.still_hard: Timing, credible promises and workforce trust remain human work. GDPR applies to employee questions; consultation and employment requirements depend on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Hear concerns, recognise implied promises and negotiate language employees and labor relations managers can trust.

ambition.what: Supervisor briefing sheet for shift huddles.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling updates toward employee listening and preparing supervisors for difficult questions. Communication and employment decision rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Make operational changes understandable to employees.
reach.learn: Audience testing, plain language and preservation of employment meaning.

reach.task: Prepare supervisor briefings and employee question summaries.
reach.learn: Confidentiality boundaries and escalation of personal cases.

evidence.claim: Briefing assembly and approval-controlled internal publication can use deterministic templates and workflow rules.
Bounded drafting can assist wording, but cannot establish employee trust or resolve employment implications.

assumptions: Approved activity updates exist separately from individual employee case files.
The labor relations manager is the assumed release approver; local delegation may differ.
Approval in s4 is consumed by publication in s5.
Time estimates retain substantial human discussion, consistent with the people and judgement priors.
Question grouping supports communication planning and does not evaluate individual employees.
Access work includes GDPR controls and works-council or employee consultation where national rules apply; elapsed consultation may exceed build effort.
unknowns: Which employee channels reach desk-based and shift workers.
The designated approver and required employee representative involvement.
Whether questions contain special-category data or personal employment disputes.
Approved retention periods and access boundaries.
Availability of interfaces for internal publication.
research_questions: Which drafting checks catch implied promises and changes in employment meaning?
How accurately can grouping preserve minority concerns without exposing individuals?
Which supervisor briefing format is easiest to use in a shift huddle?
new_work: Review wording, promises and source accuracy.
Keep templates and communication constraints current.
Handle personal questions outside the grouping flow.
Maintain access, retention and consultation records.
Check whether employee groups actually receive and understand updates.
tasks.statement: Confer with labor relations managers to develop internal communications that keep employees informed of company activities.

tasks.short: Develop, edit and approve brochures and other promotional publications.

steps.what: Agree the audience, publication purpose, message and format.
Collect current facts, approved claims, images and usage permissions.
Write and edit the publication copy.

loop.input: Publication brief, approved source pack and brand guidelines.
loop.output: Copy draft with source references for factual claims.
loop.check: Validate names and numbers against source fields; flag unsupported claims for editorial review.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section; unresolved claims return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but audience-specific explanations and editorial transitions require language generation.

steps.what: Lay out copy and images in the publication design.
Resolve factual, editorial and visual comments and approve the final proof.
Publish the approved file or release it to the print supplier.

tasks.design: Maintain approved facts, asset rights and templates in the {DOCS}, with a bounded drafting loop producing source-linked copy. A deterministic generator fills established layouts, while the {WORKFLOW} binds approval to the exact file and release destination before publishing through the {CMS} or {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts and asset permissions were scattered, while editorial changes repeatedly disturbed layouts. Bespoke document automation cost too much for small publication volumes.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can work from a controlled source pack. AI-assisted coding makes template filling, version checks and proof validation cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: A new visual concept, ambiguous claims, translation nuance and print production errors still need specialists. Template automation covers established formats more readily than bespoke design.
tasks.human_edge: Judge what deserves emphasis, what readers will understand and whether the finished publication represents the organisation honestly.

ambition.what: Accessible digital brochure variants for readers using assistive technology.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more of the week testing messages and editing arguments, with less version chasing. Within the existing publication mandate, they can prioritise audience variants; approval rights stay the same.

reach.task: Test whether a brochure's argument and evidence meet reader needs.
reach.learn: Structural editing, plain language and source verification.

reach.task: Specify a reusable accessible publication template.
reach.learn: Reading order, text hierarchy, image descriptions and print constraints.

evidence.claim: HubSpot offers branded content generation; this supports drafting feasibility, not automatic brochure approval or layout quality.
Structured content can populate established layouts with deterministic checks; the proposed implementation and time shares are estimates.
AI Act Article 50 creates transparency duties for specified AI-generated content uses; applicability must be checked for the publication.

assumptions: The initial scope is one established publication format and one language.
The layout step uses a desktop publishing system, represented by {OTHER}.
Approved claims and image rights can be recorded with owners and review dates.
GDPR applies where publications or source packs contain personal data; national rules govern any required employee consultation.
Release reuses the final-proof approval only while the file, destination and release instructions remain unchanged.
unknowns: Which layout tools support reliable template automation and export?
Who verifies technical, legal and sustainability claims?
Which accessibility standards and print specifications are required?
Which assets have valid publication and adaptation rights?
Does existing software support approval-bound release?
research_questions: Which publication format has enough recurring volume to justify a generator?
Can exported proofs preserve accessible reading order and survive supplier preflight checks?
new_work: Review generated copy for omissions, unsupported claims and tone.
Maintain source ownership, expiry dates and asset permissions.
Check layout overflow, accessibility and print readiness.
Maintain templates and investigate release failures.
tasks.statement: Design and edit promotional publications, such as brochures.

tasks.short: Guide corporate identity and ensure consistent use of logos, visual assets and signage.

steps.what: Collect current brand assets, guidelines and examples of inconsistent use.
Discuss desired identity, audience perceptions and practical constraints with stakeholders.
Choose the identity direction and brief the graphic designer.
Develop logo and signage artwork using design software in {OTHER}.
Approve artwork, usage rules and production proofs within the identity mandate.
Export approved formats and place usage packs in the shared asset library.
Inspect installed signage against approved identity standards.

tasks.design: Configure an asset library in {DOCS} with approved versions, usage rights and channel templates. Saved export presets in design software in {OTHER} generate routine variants, while {WORKFLOW} routes requests and records approval of master artwork and production proofs. Creative direction and physical inspection remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teams reused local files, requested repeated exports and could not easily identify the approved master. Identity choices and physical production quality were never reducible to file management.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned libraries, reusable templates and batch exports already exist. AI-assisted coding can cheaply connect request forms, metadata checks and approval records without introducing a generative design dependency.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctiveness, cultural meaning, stakeholder agreement and physical materials need skilled judgement. Asset rights, legacy signage and specialist production formats can make rollout expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the identity feels credible and recognisable, then resolve competing stakeholder preferences without weakening the design.

ambition.what: Self-service generation of approved branch-event signage from locked templates.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time on direction and adoption, while the designer receives fewer routine export requests. A separate delegation can let event planners generate approved variants; changing the master identity retains its existing approval route.

reach.task: Create reusable identity templates with constrained editable fields.
reach.learn: Template constraints, production specifications and accessible colour use.

reach.task: Prepare compliant event signage from approved templates.
reach.learn: Template limits, viewing distance and when to request designer review.

evidence.claim: Asset versioning, locked templates and batch exports can reduce routine identity production work.
The digest provides no documented corporate-identity case supporting automated creative direction.
Remaining effort and build ranges are estimates for a limited asset-library and template rollout.

assumptions: Time shares estimate participating roles' effort across recurring identity maintenance and occasional changes.
The substantial meeting and creative judgement priors remain reflected in the manual steps.
Design software in {OTHER} supports saved export presets.
Build ranges exclude a corporate rebrand, asset recreation and physical signage replacement.
The initial library can reuse existing approved masters and usage permissions.
unknowns: Which files are authoritative, editable and cleared for reuse?
Who can approve identity changes and production proofs?
Which signage formats and languages need templates?
What access reviews, consultation and national rules apply to the rollout?
research_questions: Which template constraints preserve brand quality while allowing useful local adaptation?
Which physical production errors escape digital proof review most often?
new_work: Maintain master assets, rights metadata and export presets.
Retire obsolete variants and handle requests outside template limits.
Review production proofs and resolve physical installation defects.
Train local users to recognise when a template no longer fits.
tasks.statement: Develop and maintain the company's corporate image and identity, which includes the use of logos and signage.

tasks.short: Develop, test and maintain crisis communication plans.

steps.what: Collect incident lessons, contact lists and existing response procedures.
Agree scenarios, escalation triggers, responsibilities and spokesperson authority.
Draft the response playbook, holding statements and question-and-answer material.

loop.input: Approved scenarios, responsibilities, procedures, facts and controlled statement templates.
loop.output: A draft playbook with conditional holding statements and explicitly unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate contacts and required sections; trace claims to facts and prevent invented incident details.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions; unsupported claims remain blank for specialist completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates generate the structure, but scenario-specific explanations and questions require language drafting.

steps.what: Run a tabletop exercise and agree corrections.
Approve the corrected plan and its authority limits.
Distribute the approved version and archive superseded copies.
Check contacts, review dates and changes that require plan revision.

tasks.design: Keep controlled plans, approved facts and contact records in the {DOCS}, with evidence collection through the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A template generator and bounded drafting loop prepare revisions; the {WORKFLOW} manages approval, controlled distribution and maintenance requests. The crisis team chooses responses and rehearses them; plan approval grants no automatic authority to publish an incident statement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans depend on dispersed operational knowledge and become stale between reviews. Generic templates cannot settle scenario choices, legal uncertainty or spokesperson authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Version control, scheduled checks and approval workflows already cover much of the maintenance. Bounded drafting can adapt approved material, while AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of assembling the package.
tasks.still_hard: Novel incidents, uncertain facts and communication under pressure remain difficult. Sensitive incident records need GDPR controls, and national rules can affect employee consultation and disclosures.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what is known, acknowledge uncertainty and balance speed, care and accountability during a crisis.

ambition.what: Run a quarterly scenario-readiness review with operational leaders.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding documents and checking lists, and more time rehearsing difficult decisions. They gain a clearer route to request corrective action; crisis and publication authority remain explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Turn the crisis playbook into usable decision cards.
reach.learn: Learn procedural writing, information sequencing and usability testing under time pressure.

reach.task: Prepare and rehearse spokesperson questions.
reach.learn: Learn interview simulation, uncertainty language and how to avoid unsupported assurances.

evidence.claim: Controlled templates, versioning, approvals and scheduled checks can support crisis-plan maintenance.
The DPD chatbot incident documents uncontrolled public language and subsequent disabling of the AI element.
The digest provides no documented case establishing automated crisis planning or response effectiveness.

assumptions: This task covers preparation, exercises and maintenance; live incident command is a separate workflow.
The company has a designated crisis lead and an agreed approval route.
No automatic meeting recording or incident publication is introduced.
The spreadsheet is a maintenance checklist rather than the authoritative plan store.
Time shares and remaining time are estimates; human exercise and approval time remain substantial.
Testing includes a tabletop exercise and checking access during an outage.
Access estimates include privacy review and any consultation required by national rules; formal processes can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which scenarios and disclosure duties apply to the organisation.
Who has authority to approve plans and live statements.
Whether emergency contacts have authoritative owners and review dates.
Whether plans must remain usable during loss of normal access.
Which national employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can participants find the correct decision route during a timed exercise?
Which statements fail review because facts or authority are unclear?
Can configured document controls meet the need before custom code is added?
Which organisational changes should trigger a maintenance request?
new_work: Review generated drafts for invented facts and false certainty.
Maintain scenarios, authority limits and approved statement components.
Verify contact ownership and resolve overdue checks.
Test controlled distribution and outage access.
Record exercise findings and verify that corrective actions close.
tasks.statement: Develop, implement, or maintain crisis communication plans.

tasks.short: Direct agencies and internal teams delivering communication strategies and public information programs.

steps.what: Agree communication outcomes, priorities, and constraints with leadership and delivery leads.
Write the delivery brief with audiences, messages, deliverables, deadlines, and acceptance criteria.

loop.input: Delivery priorities, approved facts, agreement constraints, and brief template.
loop.output: Draft delivery brief with measurable acceptance criteria and open questions.
loop.check: Check dates, required fields, factual claims, and scope against approved records; flag proposed commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing strategic choices return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Field population is deterministic, but translating varied strategic priorities into a clear narrative brief needs drafting.

steps.what: Resolve questions and agree responsibilities, scope, and delivery commitments.
Request progress updates and record blockers against the delivery plan.
Copy progress updates into a separate management summary.
Review deliverables and performance, then give corrective direction.
Approve changes within delegated scope or escalate additional cost and commitments.

tasks.design: Use the {PROJECT} as the shared delivery record, with configured update forms, reminders, deadlines, and live status views replacing separate progress summaries. A bounded drafting loop assembles briefs from approved material in the {DOCS}; people negotiate commitments, assess creative and reputational quality, and approve scope or cost changes through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency correspondence, briefs, and status reports were disconnected. Delivery direction also required negotiation and qualitative judgement that simple task tracking could not replace.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared delivery records and configured reminders can remove chasing and duplicate reporting. Bounded drafting can prepare consistent briefs without granting authority to commit spending or publish content.
tasks.still_hard: Agency cooperation, creative quality, attribution of communication outcomes, and difficult performance conversations remain costly. External access must protect confidential material and personal data under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: Giving clear direction, recognizing weak work early, managing disagreement, and knowing when to challenge or support an agency.

ambition.what: Weekly agency effort reallocation within approved scope

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing updates and rewriting status reports, and more time reviewing work before deadlines. Existing scope and spending limits remain; no new contracting rights arise.

reach.task: Compare an agency's proposed deliverables with campaign objectives and acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Creative evaluation, campaign measurement, scope control, and constructive agency feedback.

evidence.claim: Shared delivery records, configured reminders, and approval routing can reduce coordination administration.
HubSpot offers campaign planning and branded content generation, supporting brief-drafting feasibility rather than agency-management automation.
Funnel offers standardized channel data and automated reporting, which can support performance review inputs.

assumptions: Delivery leads can maintain structured progress records instead of sending free-form status messages.
Routine reminders go only to agreed project contacts and contain no new commercial commitments.
The eliminated summary duplicates a live status view; contractual reports would still need generation.
The coordination-heavy prior is retained, but routine updates are distinguished from negotiation and quality direction.
Budget holders approve only changes within their delegated limits; higher commitments follow existing escalation rules.
The access range includes external collaborator permissions, privacy review, and consultation under national rules if employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Whether agencies and internal teams will use a shared delivery record.
Which progress reports are contractually required.
Which scope, spending, and publication decisions the manager may approve.
Whether existing interfaces expose the required delivery and performance records.
research_questions: Does a shared status view remove duplicate reporting without reducing leadership visibility?
Which missing updates require a conversation rather than another reminder?
Can proposed acceptance criteria distinguish quality from simple completion?
new_work: Review generated briefs and proposed acceptance criteria.
Handle missing updates, disputed status, and delivery exceptions.
Maintain external access, reminder rules, and approval limits.
Keep shared delivery records current and archive completed work.
tasks.statement: Direct activities of external agencies, establishments, or departments that develop and implement communication strategies and information programs.

tasks.short: Prepare executive speeches and coordinate interviews, approvals, scheduling, and briefing materials.

steps.what: Agree the audience, purpose, message, and sensitive topics with the executive.
Collect approved facts, earlier remarks, and audience background.
Draft the speech in the executive's voice, with sourced claims.

loop.input: Message brief, approved source pack, speech template, and authorized examples of earlier remarks.
loop.output: Speech draft with claim references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check every factual claim against approved records; check length, prohibited topics, and executive voice.
loop.stop: One draft and two requested revisions; unsupported claims are removed or referred to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble facts but cannot produce coherent spoken language adapted to the audience and speaker.

steps.what: Rehearse the speech and resolve tone, emphasis, and difficult questions.
Approve the final speech and any commitments it contains.
Agree interview purpose, format, timing, and ground rules with the journalist.
Match availability and confirm the agreed interview arrangements.
Assemble the executive briefing with logistics, approved messages, and source facts.

tasks.design: An approved fact library in the {DOCS} feeds deterministic source-pack and briefing generators, plus a bounded speech-drafting loop. Configure availability matching in the {CALENDAR} and confirmation through the {EMAIL}, with assistant approval before sending; executive approval remains on the speech and people handle rehearsal and journalist negotiations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts, earlier remarks, and approvals were scattered across documents and correspondence. Speech quality also depends on an executive's voice and a relationship that templates alone cannot capture.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured fact records and document generation reduce assembly work. A bounded drafting loop can produce a first version while retaining source references for review.
tasks.still_hard: Executive voice, sensitive disclosures, interview ground rules, and spontaneous answers remain demanding. Confidential remarks need controlled access, and synthetic media would require a separate assessment under EU AI Act disclosure rules.
tasks.human_edge: Earning the executive's trust, coaching delivery, understanding a journalist's intent, and negotiating acceptable engagement terms.

ambition.what: Speech and interview coaching for first-time operational spokespeople

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more of the week rehearsing and coaching, with less source assembly and document formatting. Speech approval and external commitment rights remain with their current holders.

reach.task: Prepare an interview background brief and conduct a practice interview.
reach.learn: Journalistic formats, attribution terms, source verification, and spokesperson coaching.

evidence.claim: HubSpot offers branded content generation; this supports drafting feasibility, not executive-speech quality.
Source-pack assembly and availability matching can use deterministic rules when records and permissions are structured.
EU AI Act Article 50 contains disclosure duties for specified AI interactions and synthetic content.

assumptions: Speech preparation and interview coordination share a message brief but can proceed on separate timelines.
Approved fact records can carry owners, validity dates, and usage restrictions.
The source-pack generator uses approved metadata; it does not decide whether a new claim is safe.
The relationship-heavy prior is retained; drafting and scheduling support change more than negotiation or coaching.
Build ranges cover one language and a limited set of speech and briefing templates.
The access range includes privacy review and any consultation required by national rules for new recording or employee-data uses.
unknowns: Whether a maintained fact library and authorized examples of earlier remarks exist.
Which engagements require additional legal or leadership approval.
Whether external scheduling and availability access are permitted.
Which languages, confidentiality restrictions, and disclosure obligations apply to actual engagements.
research_questions: How much editing does the executive require compared with a human-written first draft?
Can fact references remain intact through revisions and final approval?
Which scheduling exceptions need assistant intervention?
new_work: Maintain fact owners, expiry dates, and permitted uses.
Review speech claims, tone, and unsupported implications.
Handle scheduling conflicts and changed interview terms.
Maintain templates and restrict access to confidential drafts.
tasks.statement: Draft speeches for company executives and arrange interviews and other forms of contact for them.

tasks.short: Build trusted relationships with clients, public officials and media, and identify business opportunities.

steps.what: Read contact history and prepare a briefing before speaking.

loop.input: Selected contact history, correspondence and approved facts.
loop.output: A sourced briefing covering commitments, open questions and relevant developments.
loop.check: Link each factual statement to its source; flag conflicting or dated information.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; missing evidence returns to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Retrieval is deterministic, but correspondence contains commitments expressed in varied language.

steps.what: Agree meeting arrangements and send the invitation.
Discuss concerns, exchange information and develop trust.
Write contact notes and record commitments.

loop.input: Manager-entered notes and existing contact identifiers.
loop.output: Proposed contact note, commitments, owners and due dates.
loop.check: Require valid contact identifiers; distinguish explicit commitments from interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous commitments remain unrecorded pending review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Short meeting notes need interpretation before they become structured commitments.

steps.what: Decide whether an opportunity merits a commercial introduction.
Send agreed follow-ups and introduce qualified opportunities to the sales team.

loop.input: Approved commitments, opportunity decision, recipient and relevant approved facts.
loop.output: A follow-up message and, where appropriate, an internal opportunity referral.
loop.check: Match promises and claims to approved inputs; verify recipient and applicable contact restrictions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims or sensitive introductions go to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relationship-specific wording varies; fixed templates cover only routine confirmations.

tasks.design: Configure contact records and follow-up tracking in the {CRM}, linked to the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. Bounded loops prepare sourced briefings, structure manager-entered notes and draft follow-ups; the manager approves record changes and outgoing messages while conducting the relationships personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact history is scattered, and extracting commitments from correspondence takes manual reading. Trust and commercial timing remain personal.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record and scheduling features handle coordination. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector work, while bounded extraction and drafting handle varied language.
tasks.still_hard: Private context, political sensitivities and unstated expectations are difficult to capture. Contact data needs a lawful purpose, limited retention and appropriate access under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: Earn trust, interpret hesitation and decide when an introduction would help or damage a relationship.

ambition.what: Maintain a structured listening programme for regional community representatives.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into meeting preparation and forgotten follow-ups; more goes into listening and introductions. Authority to make commercial commitments does not change.

reach.task: Turn recurring stakeholder concerns into research questions.
reach.learn: Learn interview coding, sampling limits and how to separate individual anecdotes from wider patterns.

evidence.claim: Contact preparation, scheduling and follow-up records can be supported without automating relationship conversations.
HubSpot provides prospecting outreach and content drafting capabilities; this does not establish relationship quality.

assumptions: The company has contact records, although important context also sits in individual mailboxes.
Time shares and remaining time are design estimates informed by the supplied priors, not measured savings.
The package excludes automatic relationship scoring and unsolicited outreach.
Access estimates include privacy review and any consultation required by national rules; formal consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which contacts and correspondence the manager may access and reuse.
Whether contact records are complete and available through supported interfaces.
Which commitments require commercial or legal approval.
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply.
research_questions: How often do briefings omit an important prior commitment?
Which follow-up messages are routine enough for configured templates?
Does preparation time fall without reducing the quality of stakeholder conversations?
new_work: Review briefings for stale or misleading context.
Approve proposed contact notes and outgoing messages.
Resolve duplicate contacts and maintain retention rules.
Maintain connectors and approved drafting templates.
tasks.statement: Establish and maintain effective working relationships with clients, government officials, and media representatives and use these relationships to develop new business opportunities.

tasks.short: Check advertising and promotion plans against public relations messages, timing and reputational risks.

steps.what: Receive campaign plans, creative materials and planned launch dates.
Compare campaign claims and dates with approved messages and planned public relations activity.

loop.input: Campaign claims, creative text, approved facts and both calendars.
loop.output: Referenced claim discrepancies and message conflicts; date clashes come from deterministic rules.
loop.check: Each finding cites both source passages; distinguish contradiction, missing evidence and stylistic difference.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass; unresolved interpretation stays with the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calendar clashes are deterministic, but implied claims and message conflicts require reading.

steps.what: Judge audience interpretation, reputational risk and strategic compatibility.
Discuss conflicts and agree changes with the advertising and promotions manager.
Record the approved decision, required changes and responsible owners.
Check revised materials and record public relations clearance.

loop.input: Revised materials and the approved list of required changes.
loop.output: Change checklist with evidence and a proposed clearance status.
loop.check: Check every required change and flag new claims; the manager grants clearance.
loop.stop: One pass per submitted revision; missing changes return to the campaign owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Required changes can alter meaning without matching exact text.

tasks.design: A review flow on {PROJECT} gathers campaign materials from {DOCS} and compares campaign dates with the public relations calendar using deterministic rules. A bounded comparison loop proposes source-linked message conflicts, while the manager judges reputational implications and negotiates changes. Approved decisions and revision checks stay in {PROJECT}, with human approval before compatibility clearance takes effect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reviews depended on emailed versions, tacit brand knowledge and manual comparison. A checklist alone could not detect conflicts in implied meaning.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned records and configurable approval flows provide the backbone. A bounded comparison loop can surface textual conflicts without deciding whether a campaign should proceed.
tasks.still_hard: Cultural interpretation, strategic trade-offs and disagreement between teams remain hard. Missing claim evidence cannot be repaired by a model.
tasks.human_edge: Anticipate how audiences will interpret a campaign and negotiate a credible compromise between commercial and reputational aims.

ambition.what: Public relations compatibility review at concept and pre-production milestones.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time comparing versions and chasing changes, and more time influencing concepts before production. Earlier review can be added to the campaign process; any right to withhold clearance requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Resolve unsupported claims before commissioning creative production.
reach.learn: Campaign economics, production lead times and acceptable alternatives.

reach.task: Test audience interpretation of disputed campaign messages.
reach.learn: Question design and the limits of small audience samples.

evidence.claim: Deterministic calendar checks and versioned decision records can remove comparison and coordination work.
Bounded text comparison can propose conflicts; strategic and reputational clearance remains a human decision.

assumptions: Campaign briefs and creative materials are available as readable, versioned documents.
Approved claims and a public relations calendar can be maintained.
The scope is compatibility review, not advertising performance attribution.
Time estimates retain the substantial judgement and coordination indicated by the priors.
The clearance gate controls an internal review status; campaign publication has its own approval.
Build ranges assume one project workspace and one document store, with access review and any applicable consultation.
unknowns: Whether public relations has formal clearance authority.
Which campaign milestones currently include compatibility review.
Where approved claims, versions and calendars are maintained.
The volume of visual claims that text extraction would miss.
Applicable access and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which comparison tests distinguish contradictions from harmless wording differences?
How should implied visual claims be presented for human review?
Does earlier review reduce late creative rework?
new_work: Maintain approved claims and review criteria.
Review proposed conflicts and dismiss false alarms.
Keep campaign versions and calendars current.
Resolve disputed findings and confirm delegated clearance authority.
Evaluate missed conflicts using completed campaign reviews.
tasks.statement: Evaluate advertising and promotion programs for compatibility with public relations efforts.

tasks.short: Build consumer and internal relationships, resolve communication gaps and coordinate agreed follow-up.

steps.what: Read incoming concerns and identify the responsible relationship owner.

loop.input: New request, fixed issue categories and an approved routing directory.
loop.output: Suggested issue category, owner and sensitivity flag.
loop.check: Validate owner against the directory; explicit sensitive categories always enter a restricted queue.
loop.stop: One classification per request; ambiguity, sensitive content or conflicting routes go to human triage.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use deterministic routing for known forms; varied free-text messages need bounded classification.

steps.what: Gather relevant history, approved facts and the parties' stated concerns.

loop.input: Authorised case history, approved facts and source messages.
loop.output: Source-linked brief separating facts, each party's account and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Check source links, access boundaries and factual dates; prohibit inferred motives or employee scores.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per case; disputed or unavailable history stays explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Summarising differing accounts requires reading narrative text; fixed fields cover only known facts.

steps.what: Listen to the parties, clarify misunderstandings and discuss possible resolutions.
Agree actions, responsible owners and limits on what can be promised.
Write and send the agreed summary and follow-up commitments.

loop.input: Human-entered agreed action plan, approved facts and recipient list.
loop.output: Proposed summary with owners, dates and explicitly agreed commitments.
loop.check: Match every commitment to the action plan; manager checks wording and recipients before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous commitments require human rewriting and approval.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but a tactful account of the agreement needs contextual wording.

steps.what: Check outstanding commitments and remind responsible owners.

tasks.design: A case register in {WORKFLOW} separates consumer and internal requests by access rules, using bounded classification only where routing rules are insufficient. Source-linked briefs from {DOCS} and authorised records in {CRM} prepare human conversations; approved summaries go through {EMAIL}, and {PROJECT} tracks commitments and internal reminders. The system proposes closure for the relationship owner to verify.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relationship history and promises lived in private mail threads. Software could track tickets, but incomplete accounts and sensitive context made automated responses unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured registers, access controls and reminders handle the coordination. Bounded summarisation can prepare conversations and correspondence without giving software authority to negotiate.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, disputed accounts, power imbalances and promises requiring another department's approval remain difficult. Sensitive employee or consumer information requires careful access and retention choices.
tasks.human_edge: Hear what is being left unsaid, recognise unfairness and build agreement that the parties actually accept.

ambition.what: Monthly cross-branch listening clinic with tracked responses to recurring communication barriers.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less history gathering and reminder chasing, leaving more time for difficult conversations and early relationship repair. The manager gains no authority to make commitments beyond existing delegated limits.

reach.task: Coordinate routine relationship cases and prepare neutral conversation briefs.
reach.learn: Neutral summarisation, confidentiality boundaries and escalation judgement.

reach.task: Turn anonymised recurring concerns into questions for a listening study.
reach.learn: Qualitative coding, sampling limits and avoiding identification of individuals.

evidence.claim: A shared webcare inbox and monitoring dashboards demonstrate available consumer-intake capabilities, not automated relationship repair.
A documented chatbot failure supports keeping sensitive public replies and commitments under human control.
GDPR requirements apply to personal data; employee consultation and representation requirements depend on national rules and implementation.
The proposed bounded briefs, effort estimates and implementation ranges require local validation.

assumptions: Time shares estimate participating roles' effort for relationship cases handled by communications.
Human conversation and agreement occupy most effort, consistent with the relationship prior.
Internal employee cases use restricted records rather than broadly accessible customer records.
The initial pilot excludes grievances, disciplinary matters and negotiations outside the manager's mandate.
No meeting recording, sentiment scoring of employees or autonomous public reply is required.
Access time includes consultation screening; formal processes under national rules can exceed the range.
unknowns: Which consumer and internal issues belong to communications rather than another function?
Which case histories can be accessed and for how long?
Who can authorise commitments outside the manager's limits?
What employee consultation and national rules apply?
What evidence is required before a relationship owner closes a case?
research_questions: How well do brief reviewers detect omitted disagreements and misleadingly neutral summaries?
Which closure checks distinguish completed actions from restored trust?
new_work: Review routing suggestions and keep the ownership directory current.
Correct incomplete briefs and remove unnecessary personal information.
Approve recipient-specific summaries and check commitments against delegated limits.
Resolve overdue actions, verify closure and maintain access and retention rules.
tasks.statement: Facilitate consumer relations or the relationship between parts of the company, such as the managers and employees, or different branch offices.

tasks.short: Develop and approve policies and procedures for public information programs with communications leadership.

steps.what: Review existing policies, incidents, and gaps in public information handling.

loop.input: Current policy versions, incident records, and policy change request.
loop.output: Candidate gap assessment linking each finding to a passage or incident.
loop.check: Require source references; distinguish explicit contradictions from inferred gaps; manager validates material findings.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document set; missing or conflicting evidence goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Version comparison finds changed text but cannot connect varied incident narratives to policy gaps.

steps.what: Discuss objectives, responsibilities, and practical constraints with communications leadership.
Choose disclosure boundaries, approval responsibilities, and escalation rules.
Draft policy clauses, operating procedures, and handling examples.

loop.input: Chosen policy decisions, requirements, approved reference material, and policy template.
loop.output: Policy draft and a requirement-to-clause map.
loop.check: Check every requirement has a clause; flag conflicting duties and unsupported legal statements for specialist review.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions; unresolved policy choices return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates support structure, but varied requirements need readable clauses and context-specific examples.

steps.what: Review legal duties, privacy implications, and operational feasibility with affected teams.
Approve the policy, accountable roles, and effective date.
Publish the approved version and notify affected teams.

tasks.design: Use versioned records in the {DOCS} and an approval flow in the {WORKFLOW} to manage policy changes. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare a gap assessment and mapped clauses, while people choose policy positions, complete specialist review, and approve the effective version; publication and notifications then run automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy work mixed document administration with unresolved organizational choices. Templates could not reconcile incident narratives, competing responsibilities, and inconsistent clauses.
tasks.enabler_now: Version control, requirement mapping, and approval routing are established capabilities. Bounded text processing can prepare comparisons and drafts without selecting the organization's policy position.
tasks.still_hard: Leadership agreement, legal interpretation, and workable escalation boundaries remain human work. GDPR, relevant EU AI Act duties, and applicable national rules must be assessed against the actual program.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing openness, confidentiality, speed, and accountability, then securing agreement from people who must apply the policy.

ambition.what: Scenario-based public-information playbook for frontline team leads

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling policy text and more time testing difficult scenarios with affected teams. No new policy approval rights arise; communications leadership retains final approval.

reach.task: Turn approved disclosure rules into usable procedures and handling examples.
reach.learn: Task analysis, controlled terminology, version management, and procedure usability testing.

evidence.claim: Policy drafting can be assisted, but organizational policy choices and legal review remain human responsibilities.
EU AI Act Article 50 is relevant when policies govern specified AI interactions or synthetic public content.
The digest supplies no documented case demonstrating end-to-end automation of public-information policy formulation.

assumptions: A communications leadership role can approve policies within an established governance structure.
The solution supports a bounded policy family rather than a company-wide compliance transformation.
The near-total-automation prior is too strong: choosing policy positions and securing agreement consume substantial effort.
Build ranges estimate one initial policy family, including versioning and approval routing.
The access range includes privacy review and any employee consultation required by national rules; a contested process can take longer.
unknowns: Which body has final policy approval authority.
Whether current policies, incidents, and review records are complete and accessible.
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed policy changes.
Whether affected teams can participate in scenario testing during rollout.
research_questions: Does the draft preserve important exceptions and distinctions from the approved requirements?
Can frontline teams correctly apply the procedure to ambiguous requests?
Which policy changes need consultation before approval or implementation?
new_work: Validate extracted gaps and requirement-to-clause mappings.
Resolve conflicting clauses and unsupported legal statements.
Maintain policy versions, effective dates, and review schedules.
Refresh handling examples after incidents and rule changes.
tasks.statement: Formulate policies and procedures related to public information programs, working with public relations executives.

tasks.short: Identify audiences, choose communication approaches and deliver a communication plan.

steps.what: Gather audience research, stakeholder concerns and previous campaign results.
Summarise audience needs, barriers and communication preferences.

loop.input: Research extracts, stakeholder feedback and dated campaign results.
loop.output: A sourced assessment of audience needs, barriers and evidence gaps.
loop.check: Trace findings to sources; separate measured behaviour from inference and flag small samples.
loop.stop: One synthesis and one correction pass; unsupported audience claims remain open questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Qualitative research uses varied language that fixed categories alone cannot reliably interpret.

steps.what: Choose priority audiences, objectives, messages and channels.
Write the plan, including schedule, responsibilities and measures.

loop.input: Chosen audiences, objectives, messages, channels, approved facts and planning template.
loop.output: A draft plan with a structured schedule, responsibilities and measurement definitions.
loop.check: Validate required fields, dates and budget totals deterministically; link claims to approved facts.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions; unresolved strategy or factual gaps return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: The schedule is deterministic, but the narrative must explain choices for this audience and context.

steps.what: Approve the plan and its resource commitments.
Publish approved materials and coordinate channel delivery.
Compare results with objectives and flag changes for the next plan.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles permitted research and results from the {CRM}, {SOCIAL} and {BI}; bounded loops draft audience assessments and plans in the {DOCS}. Approved plans create delivery tasks in the {PROJECT}, with release approval in the {CMS}, {SOCIAL} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}. Configured reporting returns results against the plan's objectives.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research and channel results use different formats, while each plan needs a context-specific narrative. Manual copying separates strategy from delivery.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors and configured publishing workflows handle collection and delivery. Bounded synthesis can draft sourced assessments, and AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of joining the pieces.
tasks.still_hard: Audience representation, causal attribution and message choice remain uncertain. GDPR, applicable ePrivacy rules and EU AI Act transparency duties must be reflected in channel and content rules.
tasks.human_edge: Choose whom to prioritise, hear excluded perspectives and judge whether a message deserves public attention.

ambition.what: Create an accessible communication plan for people who do not use the main digital channels.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling plans and more time testing audience assumptions. They can propose channel changes sooner; spending and publication authority remain subject to existing approval limits.

reach.task: Test whether the proposed audience groups reflect real needs.
reach.learn: Learn sampling, qualitative coding and practical message testing.

reach.task: Adapt campaign landing pages for underserved audiences.
reach.learn: Learn accessible content structure and how to validate comprehension with users.

evidence.claim: Coosto provides social listening, trending-news alerts and dashboards that can supply audience evidence.
Funnel provides channel connectors, standardised data and automated reporting.
HubSpot provides campaign planning and branded content drafting capabilities.
These capabilities support plan preparation; they do not establish the best audience or prove communication impact.

assumptions: Existing research is available; collection automation does not replace new interviews or surveys.
The spreadsheet reconciles cross-channel measures rather than serving as the main publishing tool.
Time shares cover the end-to-end task, including specialist delivery and management approval.
Remaining time and build ranges are estimates, not results from the cited products.
Publishing requires approval of the actual content and recipient scope, beyond approval of the plan.
Access work includes permitted contact use, objection handling and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Which audience groups are currently underrepresented in research.
Which channels expose usable interfaces and consistent measures.
Whether approved content, contact permissions and objections are recorded reliably.
Who can approve budgets, sensitive claims and public release.
Which national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can each audience finding be traced to sufficiently recent evidence?
Which measures reflect understanding or behaviour rather than exposure alone?
Which draft sections need substantial manager revision?
Can configured connectors cover the required sources before custom integration is built?
new_work: Review audience summaries for unsupported generalisations.
Maintain research provenance, metric definitions and channel mappings.
Check contact restrictions and approve publication batches.
Repair failed deliveries and reconcile missing results.
Refresh templates and retire outdated approved claims.
tasks.statement: Identify main client groups and audiences, determine the best way to communicate publicity information to them, and develop and implement a communication plan.

tasks.short: Preserve, organise and retrieve company communications and historical records.

steps.what: Collect final publications, coverage, photographs and historical records from contributors.
Enter received items into a separate archive tracking workbook.
Identify dates, subjects, owners, rights and record categories.

loop.input: Items missing metadata after deterministic extraction, approved taxonomy and source text.
loop.output: Suggested categories and source-linked descriptive metadata; unresolved fields remain blank.
loop.check: Validate schema, dates and taxonomy values; review uncertain fields and all proposed rights information.
loop.stop: One classification and one schema repair per item; unresolved items enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Source metadata and rules handle current records, but inconsistent legacy text needs contextual interpretation.

steps.what: File records, apply metadata and maintain the searchable catalogue.
Resolve uncertain ownership, access restrictions and retention treatment.
Find requested records and provide permitted copies or links.
Review records due for disposal and authorise eligible deletions.

tasks.design: Use the {DOCS} as the archive catalogue and remove the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} register; deterministic intake preserves provenance, versions and existing access restrictions. A bounded loop proposes missing descriptive metadata, while the {WORKFLOW} routes rights and retention exceptions to the records manager and gates deletion; permission-aware search handles routine retrieval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Final files arrived inconsistently, legacy descriptions were incomplete and archive tracking duplicated the document store. Rights and retention exceptions could not safely be inferred from filenames.
tasks.enabler_now: Document-store metadata, search and retention features already cover much of the task. AI-assisted coding lowers connector costs, and bounded classification can help with poorly described legacy material.
tasks.still_hard: Historical authenticity, unclear ownership, legal holds and preservation formats remain difficult. Physical collections and damaged media need separate handling.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise historically significant material and resolve ambiguous rights, context and preservation choices.

ambition.what: A permission-aware self-service catalogue of approved historical communications.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time collecting, indexing and answering routine requests, and more time curating important records. They can manage catalogue quality and recommend preservation priorities; rights, retention and access exceptions stay with the designated decision makers.

reach.task: Assemble a verified historical timeline for a publication.
reach.learn: Provenance, contextual verification and the difference between evidence and recollection.

evidence.claim: Document stores commonly provide metadata, permissions, versioning and search; the digest contains no archive-specific product evidence.
Rules can handle structured intake, with bounded classification reserved for missing descriptive metadata.
GDPR affects personal-data access and retention. Archival purpose does not automatically justify unlimited retention.

assumptions: The archive is primarily digital communications material, rather than a regulated corporate records repository.
The representative current process includes a duplicate intake workbook; eliminating it depends on confirming that duplication.
The first build covers selected sources and a pilot collection, not complete historical migration.
Records retain source permissions; uncertain items enter restricted staging before catalogue release.
Model suggestions cannot establish usage rights, release legal holds or authorise deletion.
National rules determine employee consultation where archive access or monitoring changes.
unknowns: What archive volumes, formats and physical holdings exist?
Does the tracking workbook contain information absent from the document store?
Which retention schedules, legal holds and historical-preservation obligations apply?
Who may approve access changes, rights exceptions and disposal?
Can source permissions and provenance be preserved through intake?
Does the document store support required preservation and export formats?
research_questions: Which metadata fields most improve retrieval on a representative sample?
Can duplicate detection distinguish identical files from historically meaningful versions?
What migration approach preserves provenance without widening access?
new_work: Review uncertain metadata and rights suggestions.
Resolve intake failures, duplicates and permission mismatches.
Maintain taxonomy, retention mappings and source connectors.
Review disposal queues and preserve audit evidence.
Check retrieval quality and file readability over time.
tasks.statement: Maintain company archives.

tasks.short: Plan communications spending, track commitments and secure budget changes.

steps.what: Retrieve communications actuals, purchase commitments and the approved budget.
Reconcile actuals and commitments with the communications budget tracker.
Estimate remaining costs and compare spending scenarios.
Discuss trade-offs with campaign owners and agree proposed spending priorities.
Approve, reject or return the proposed budget change under delegated limits.
Update the budget tracker and notify campaign owners of approved allocations.

tasks.design: Configured extracts from {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} feed deterministic reconciliation and scenario calculations on {DATA_PLATFORM}, displayed in {BI}. An approval flow in {WORKFLOW} records budget decisions and updates allocations, replacing the duplicate tracker in {SPREADSHEET}. Purchasing and payment retain their separate authorisations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actuals, commitments and agency estimates used different categories and reporting dates. Reconciliation depended on local knowledge, while budget decisions remained in mail threads.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting interfaces and approval features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes category mapping, reconciliation rules and scenario views cheaper to assemble; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Late invoices, uncertain agency scope and shared costs can distort forecasts. Deciding which communications activity to stop remains a judgement about priorities and reputation.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate credible trade-offs and protect essential communications capacity when returns are difficult to quantify.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on releasing or retaining uncommitted communications contingency.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconciling trackers and more time challenging commitments and scenarios. Any right to move money still depends on explicit delegated limits.

reach.task: Compare shared campaign spending options before committing funds.
reach.learn: Commitment accounting, scenario assumptions and the limits of communications attribution.

reach.task: Forecast event commitments against communications allocations.
reach.learn: Cancellation terms, accrual timing and estimate uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Standardised channel data and automated reporting are available today; this does not establish ledger reconciliation or PR budget optimisation.
Budget reconciliation, scenario calculations and approval routing can use deterministic rules.
The proposed time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Time shares estimate participating roles' task effort and require local measurement.
A spreadsheet ties finance extracts to the communications plan; the ledger remains in {ERP}.
The manager retains substantial decision and negotiation work, consistent with the judgement prior.
The initial build covers one budget hierarchy and existing finance approval limits.
Consultation review is included in access time; employee-level performance scoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Are purchase commitments and accruals available alongside posted actuals?
Which costs are shared across communications, marketing and events?
What budget transfers can each role approve?
Which interfaces, financial access controls and national consultation rules apply?
research_questions: Which reconciliation rules distinguish duplicate commitments from genuine remaining costs?
Which forecast presentation makes uncertain estimates clearest to budget holders?

Maintain category mappings, approval limits and scenario assumptions.
Check data freshness and reconcile dashboard totals to finance reports.
Review failed allocation updates and retain decision history.
tasks.statement: Manage communications budgets.

tasks.short: Organise internal courses that improve employees' communication skills.

steps.what: Discuss communication gaps and select course outcomes with team managers.
Agree trainers, dates, rooms and course capacity.
Prepare exercises, examples and participant materials.

loop.input: Course outcomes, approved communication guidance and anonymised scenario requirements.
loop.output: Exercise drafts and facilitator notes in the course template.
loop.check: Trace factual guidance to sources; trainer checks suitability, realism and absence of identifiable incidents.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per exercise; unsuitable material returns to the trainer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reusable templates organise the course, but tailored role-play scenarios require contextual writing.

steps.what: Review materials and approve them for the course.
Enrol participants and send joining instructions and reminders.
Facilitate practice, discuss difficult situations and give individual feedback.
Record participation and review feedback to revise the next course.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling, enrolment, reminders and completion records in the {LMS} and {CALENDAR}. A bounded drafting loop prepares exercises in the {DOCS} for trainer approval, while a course dashboard supports human decisions about future content.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course administration crossed calendars, messages and learning records. Relevant exercises still required someone who understood internal communication situations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning features handle most administration. A small drafting loop can adapt approved guidance into practice scenarios without automating facilitation.
tasks.still_hard: Psychological safety, candid feedback and transfer into everyday behaviour remain human work. Attendance and satisfaction are weak measures of communication improvement.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation, adapt exercises and help employees practise difficult conversations without embarrassment.

ambition.what: Short communication practice sessions for shift-based employees.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time on enrolment and preparation and more time observing practice and improving course relevance. They can propose new cohorts within the agreed learning budget; authority over employee performance does not change.

reach.task: Coach employees through a simulated media enquiry.
reach.learn: Facilitation, constructive feedback and boundaries for spokesperson authority.

evidence.claim: Learning systems commonly support enrolment, reminders and completion records; the digest supplies no documented communication-course case.
A bounded model can draft practice scenarios from approved guidance, subject to trainer review.
GDPR applies to participant records and feedback. Employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed data use.

An existing {LMS} is available; replacing it is outside the estimate.
Routine enrolments follow agreed eligibility rules, with exceptions sent to the coordinator.
Drafting uses anonymised scenarios and does not score employees.
The consultation range includes reviewing employee-data uses; a formal national process may exceed it.

Who owns enrolment eligibility and attendance corrections?
Which feedback may be retained, and who may see it?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
Can shift-based employees access paid learning time and suitable devices?

What observable practice would show improvement without ranking individual employees?

Handle enrolment exceptions and incorrect completion records.
Maintain course templates and scheduling rules.
Review aggregate feedback and test whether course changes improve practice.

tasks.short: Plan and run events that attract relevant public and media attention.

steps.what: Agree the event purpose, audience, message and success measures.
Build the schedule, responsibilities and supplier cost estimate.
Approve supplier commitments and the event budget.
Prepare invitations, registration pages and media packs.
Approve materials and send invitations to the selected contacts.
Coordinate suppliers, speakers, guests and media during the event.
Review coverage, attendance, feedback and spending against the event brief.

tasks.design: Configure reusable event plans and registration flows in the {PROJECT} and {WORKFLOW}; generate invitation and media-pack drafts from approved facts in the {DOCS}. Route supplier commitments and publication through their respective approvers, then join attendance, coverage and {ERP} actuals in the {BI}.

reach.learn: Critical-path scheduling, venue constraints and escalation triggers.

Invitations that constitute direct marketing require applicable ePrivacy consent or exception checks.

The company has approved facts and reusable brand templates.
The first build covers one recurring event format.
GDPR applies to guest and media-contact records. National rules determine any employee consultation needed.

Who approves event spending, publications and recipient lists?

Which event activities involve employee monitoring or require consultation?

Which measures would distinguish useful media engagement from attendance alone?

Resolve registration, supplier and coverage-matching exceptions.
Maintain event templates, connectors and permission rules.
Check that reported results use consistent definitions.

tasks.short: Monitor external trends, assess their implications, and brief leadership on emerging issues.

steps.what: Search news monitoring services and social feeds for relevant developments.
Read coverage and assemble a shortlist with source links.

loop.input: Deduplicated source collection and watchlist.
loop.output: Candidate trend shortlist with relevance reasons and source links.
loop.check: Require a retrievable source for each item; sample excluded items for missed signals.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair per batch; unreadable or disputed items enter a review queue.

Write a concise briefing with evidence, implications, and response options.

loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims remain flagged for manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure but cannot summarize varied coverage into readable, contextual prose.

Circulate the approved briefing and record follow-up owners.

tasks.short: Commission and oversee videos, approve distribution, and maintain an accessible library with rights and expiry records.

steps.what: Define the audience, purpose, story and proposed distribution channels.
Agree the crew, schedule, locations and production plan.
Verify participant releases, asset licences and permitted distribution.
Capture interviews and scenes using camera equipment.
Edit the story, sound and visuals in video editing tools.
Prepare and check captions in video editing tools.

loop.input: Audio from the review cut and an approved names glossary.
loop.output: Timed caption draft with uncertain passages marked.
loop.check: Validate timestamp order and reading length; an editor checks speech, names and meaningful sounds.

Catalogue video files, rights, captions and publication links.

Approved packages publish through {CMS} and {SOCIAL}, while the catalogue replaces the separate {SPREADSHEET} and raises rights-expiry alerts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Production coordination, rights paperwork and the library were disconnected. Creative filming and editing also depend on people and judgement, so automating the whole task was unrealistic.
tasks.enabler_now: Encoding presets, structured asset records and publishing workflows already exist. AI-assisted coding can connect them faster, and bounded transcription can reduce caption preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Story quality, interview trust, sound quality and licence interpretation remain demanding. GDPR applies to identifiable participants; applicable EU AI Act transparency duties need checking for synthetic or manipulated media.
tasks.human_edge: Elicit credible interviews, choose a truthful story and judge whether the finished video represents people fairly.

ambition.what: Searchable library of captioned, rights-cleared video excerpts.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing files, arranging routine production details and maintaining the catalogue. More time can go to story selection and reuse planning; commissioning and release rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Prepare consistent titles and graphics for video reuse.
reach.learn: Motion readability, channel formats and safe placement of captions.

reach.task: Prepare translated captions for approved videos.
reach.learn: Timing constraints, terminology and verification of translated claims.

reach.task: Find rights-cleared excerpts for press and internal communications.
reach.learn: Licence scope, expiry and context-preserving reuse.

evidence.claim: Spotler provides social publishing; this supports distribution capability, not automated video production.
Encoding presets, structured catalogues and expiry alerts can handle routine video administration deterministically.
Transcription can prepare captions for review, while filming, creative editing and rights interpretation remain human-led.

assumptions: A mid-size company normally commissions or coordinates producers and editors rather than operating a dedicated film department.
Production time shares include delegated work; manager-specific savings depend on their hands-on involvement.
A spreadsheet catalogue is typical where the document store lacks usable asset metadata.
OTHER covers camera equipment, video editing tools and video encoding tools.
Configured exports use approved framing presets; creative reframing returns to the editor.
Publication approval in s8 is consumed by the gate in s9.
The library serves approved internal users and does not identify people through biometric analysis.
Build ranges cover the workflow and library, not shooting a film; access, participant permissions and applicable employee consultation are included.
Synthetic media is optional and requires applicable transparency checks before release.
unknowns: Who performs filming, editing and captioning today.
Whether existing editing tools support batch exports and caption import.
Which publishing channels expose suitable interfaces.
The completeness and legal scope of participant releases and asset licences.
Whether employee footage requires consultation under national rules.
Library size, storage needs and the condition of legacy rights records.
research_questions: Which caption errors survive automated checks and require focused human review?
Can channel presets preserve framing and caption readability across representative footage?
Which catalogue fields make rights-cleared excerpts easy to retrieve?
How should unknown legacy rights block reuse without hiding useful records?

Maintain encoding presets and publishing connections.
Complete missing rights metadata and handle expiry alerts.
Check synthetic-media disclosures where applicable.
