Handle failed publication and withdrawal requests.
tasks.statement: Produce films and other video products, regulate their distribution, and operate film library.

tasks.short: Answer requests about organisational activities using verified facts, appropriate disclosure and personal judgement.

steps.what: Read the incoming enquiry and identify its topic, deadline and requester.

loop.input: Incoming enquiry and approved routing categories.
loop.output: Request record with topic, quoted deadline and uncertainty flag.
loop.check: Preserve the original message; validate fields; route uncertain or sensitive requests to a person.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt; missing or conflicting fields trigger manual intake.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text enquiries express topics and deadlines in varied ways.

steps.what: Find current approved facts and supporting documents.
Clarify intent and agree disclosure limits with the requester or relevant subject owner.
Draft a response from the agreed brief and approved facts.

loop.input: Response brief and dated, source-linked fact pack.
loop.output: Response draft with claim references and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Every factual claim needs an approved source; unsupported claims and disclosure conflicts block dispatch.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction attempt; unresolved claims return to the subject owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: The response must address varied questions in natural language.

steps.what: Approve wording, factual accuracy and disclosure.
Send the approved response to the requester.
File the response and update the enquiry log.

tasks.design: An intake flow on {WORKFLOW} turns enquiries from {EMAIL} into request records and retrieves approved, dated facts from {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares source-linked responses; the public relations manager handles clarification and disclosure decisions before approving dispatch through {EMAIL}. The same flow maintains the enquiry log without a separate {SPREADSHEET}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved facts were scattered, expiry was unclear, and each response needed contextual writing. Connecting records and approval states required bespoke work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building retrieval, templates and connectors. Bounded drafting can handle varied wording once approved facts are organised.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive questions, ambiguous intent and fast-changing facts still require people. GDPR purpose, access and retention requirements apply to requester records.
tasks.human_edge: Understand why someone is asking, preserve trust and decide what can responsibly be disclosed.

ambition.what: Source-linked background briefing for community journalists.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less searching, drafting and logging, with more time for difficult enquiries and background briefings. No decision rights change automatically; disclosure authority remains with the designated approver.

reach.task: Maintain the approved facts used for media enquiries.
reach.learn: Source provenance, expiry dates and escalation criteria.

reach.task: Turn technical activity updates into public explanations.
reach.learn: Plain-language explanation without changing the underlying claim.

evidence.claim: Coosto provides a shared webcare inbox and monitoring; this supports intake, not automatic sensitive disclosure.
Source-linked retrieval, bounded drafting and approval-controlled dispatch are proposed design choices.
DPD disabled an AI chatbot element after offensive responses, illustrating the cost of uncontrolled public answers.

assumptions: Most written enquiries arrive through a shared mailbox; some require a clarification call.
A spreadsheet enquiry log is typical glue where no shared request record exists.
Only facts approved for external use enter the answer desk.
Approval in s5 is the gate consumed by dispatch in s6; it is not a second approval.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates. The judgement and relationship priors limit full automation.
Build ranges assume one mailbox and one document store, including access and any applicable consultation.
unknowns: Where approved facts are stored and who can release them.
The share of routine, sensitive and conversational enquiries.
Whether mailbox and document interfaces are available.
Existing approval, retention and requester identity requirements.
research_questions: How reliably can retrieval exclude expired or superseded facts?
Which test enquiries expose unsupported claims or missed disclosure limits?
When does source-linked drafting save enough review time to justify its cost?
new_work: Maintain approved facts, source links and expiry dates.
Review drafts and handle uncertain intake records.
Monitor dispatch failures and approval-state integrity.
Maintain routing categories, access controls and retention rules.
tasks.statement: Respond to requests for information about employers' activities or status.

tasks.short: Create and publish press releases, media kits and corporate web content.

steps.what: Request facts, quotes and supporting material from subject experts.

loop.input: Authorised source material and a fixed fact-pack schema.
loop.output: Source-linked facts, quotes and missing-information flags.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each claim; verify quotes exactly and flag contradictions.
loop.stop: Two extraction passes per pack; unresolved facts return to the subject expert.
loop.why_not_simpler: Facts arrive in differently structured documents and messages; fixed fields alone miss relevant passages.

steps.what: Agree the news angle, audience and timing with the subject expert.
Write the release, media background and web copy.

loop.input: Reviewed fact pack, editorial direction, brand guidelines and channel templates.
loop.output: Draft release, media background and web copy with claim references.
loop.check: Check names, dates, figures, quotes and links against sources; manager reviews tone and implications.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per channel; unsupported claims are withheld for human rewriting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative structure and audience-specific wording need language generation; layout and factual fields remain deterministic.

steps.what: Review claims, permissions and reputational implications before approving the content.
Assemble branded release files, media assets and downloadable background documents.
Send the approved release and media-kit link to selected media contacts.
Publish approved web pages and intranet updates, then check their appearance.

tasks.design: A structured brief in {WORKFLOW} gathers source material from {DOCS}; bounded extraction and drafting produce source-linked content for review. Deterministic templates assemble the media kit, while configured flows prepare distribution through {EMAIL} and publication through {CMS}. Approval binds the exact content version, recipients, channels and timing; changes invalidate it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts, permissions and revisions were scattered across messages and documents. Templates handled formatting but could not reliably turn mixed source material into a useful narrative.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded language models can extract and draft against supplied sources. Existing publishing controls and AI-assisted coding reduce the effort of connecting intake, templates and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Newsworthiness, sensitive omissions, quotation permission and reputational consequences need judgement. Multilingual nuance and unusual page layouts add review effort.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what deserves attention, challenge weak claims and understand how journalists or employees will interpret the announcement.

ambition.what: Accessible plain-language announcement summaries for employees outside office roles.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling files and copying text toward editorial direction and source relationships. Publication authority stays with the designated approver; software creates no additional decision rights.

reach.task: Adapt an approved announcement into audience-specific summaries.
reach.learn: Plain-language editing, source attribution and accessible content structure.

reach.task: Improve reusable newsroom and intranet page templates.
reach.learn: Content hierarchy, accessibility checks and responsive preview review.

evidence.claim: Branded content drafting is available today; this supports drafting feasibility, not factual reliability.
Configured email journeys and social publishing support controlled distribution.
Source-linked extraction, version-bound approvals and the proposed effort ranges are design estimates.
Article 50 transparency duties require checking when publishing covered synthetic content; AI assistance alone does not determine every duty.

assumptions: Time shares estimate participating roles' task effort, not measured shares of the manager's week.
The initial build covers one language, a small template set and existing publishing channels.
Drafting is substantial, but the creation prior does not make editorial judgement or publication approval disappear.
Existing templates can support accessible output after validation.
unknowns: Which channels provide suitable draft, approval and scheduling controls?
Who approves sensitive claims, quotes and publication timing?
Which source documents, media contacts and assets may be processed?
What consultation, access approval and national rules apply?
research_questions: How reliably do source-linked drafts preserve qualifications and quotations in the required languages?
Which template checks best detect accessibility and rendering failures before publication?
new_work: Review source links and resolve missing or conflicting facts.
Maintain templates, brand rules and approved claim records.
Handle failed sends, publication errors and changed approvals.
Review applicable content transparency and recipient-handling requirements.
tasks.statement: Write interesting and effective press releases, prepare information for media kits, and develop and maintain company internet or intranet web pages.
